original_question:
Let ψ be a function in L2(R). For integers j,k ∈ Z, define the dyadic dilates and translates
ψ_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x − k). Call ψ an orthonormal wavelet if the collection {ψ_{j,k} : j,k ∈ Z} forms an orthonormal basis of L2(R).

Consider the set of all orthonormal wavelets as a subset of the unit sphere in L2(R). Is this set path connected in the L2(R) norm, meaning that for any two orthonormal wavelets ψ0 and ψ1 there exists a continuous map Ψ:[0,1]→L2(R) (continuous in the L2 norm) with Ψ(0)=ψ0, Ψ(1)=ψ1, and Ψ(t) an orthonormal wavelet for every t ∈ [0,1]?
target_in_paper: Section 2.1, Problem 2.1: the connectivity problem for the full collection of one-dimensional dyadic orthonormal wavelets in L^2(ℝ), namely whether that collection, viewed as a subset of the unit sphere of L^2(ℝ), is path connected in the L^2(ℝ)-norm.
correct_elements: Your draft matches the paper's target essentially verbatim. It uses the exact dyadic wavelet system from Definition 2.1, works in the correct ambient space L^2(ℝ), asks about the full class of orthonormal wavelets rather than a narrower subclass, keeps the unit-sphere viewpoint from Problem 2.1, and states path connectedness in the L^2-norm topology.
refined_question: In the classical one-dimensional dyadic setting, let ψ ∈ L^2(ℝ) and define ψ_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2}ψ(2^j x − k) for j,k ∈ ℤ. Call ψ an orthonormal wavelet if {ψ_{j,k} : j,k ∈ ℤ} is an orthonormal basis of L^2(ℝ). Is the collection of all orthonormal wavelets, viewed as a subset of the unit sphere of L^2(ℝ), path connected in the L^2(ℝ)-norm topology?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper's main connectivity question for one-dimensional dyadic wavelets, stated explicitly in Section 2.1 as Problem 2.1 on page 1. The needed notation is exactly the definition of an orthonormal wavelet given in Definition 2.1 in Section 2 on page 1. The nearby context confirms that this is the correct target: Theorem 2.2 gives a positive answer only for MRA wavelets (Section 2.1, page 1), Theorem 2.3 gives a positive answer only for MSF wavelets (Section 2.1, pages 1–2), and Conjecture 2.1 is a different, narrower statement about connectivity within a fixed wavelet dimension function (Section 2.1, page 2), proposed as evidence toward Problem 2.1 rather than as a restatement of it. So the paper-faithful refinement is simply Problem 2.1 written in stand-alone form using Definition 2.1.
